blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Transport and commuters’ groups are urging six Metro Manila local government units (LGUs) to delay or clarify the return of the no-contact apprehension policy (NCAP) on Oct. 5, citing concerns over implementation, due process and added costs for motorists. The policy will cover Manila, Muntinlupa, Parañaque, Quezon City, San Juan and Valenzuela. Transport group Manibela urged the LGUs to defer implementation, citing high fuel prices and rising costs of goods and services. “We are calling on all local government units (LGUs) implementing the NCAP to temporarily suspend its enforcement due to the ongoing oil crisis, with fuel prices […]...
